blocks.content: The CAG submits three audit reports to the President: audit report on appropriation accounts, audit report on finance accounts, and audit report on public undertakings.

rows: Compares the actual expenditure incurred against the expenditure sanctioned by Parliament through the Appropriation Act.
Presents a comprehensive account of the annual receipts and disbursements of the Union Government.
Evaluates the financial health, commercial performance, and management efficiency of Central Public Sector Enterprises.

items: Article 151 mandates the submission of CAG audit reports to the President (for Centre) and Governor (for States).
The Public Accounts Committee (PAC) acts as a guide, friend, and philosopher to the CAG during the examination of reports.
Questions often distinguish between Appropriation Accounts (expenditure vs. grant) and Finance Accounts (annual receipts and disbursements).

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The CAG submits three audit reports to the President: Audit Report on Appropriation Accounts, Audit Report on Finance Accounts, and Audit Report on Public Undertakings.
The President causes these reports to be laid before both Houses of Parliament.
The Public Accounts Committee (PAC) examines the CAG's audit reports and submits its findings to Parliament.
In the case of states, the CAG submits audit reports to the Governor, who lays them before the State Legislature.
